endorsements.quote: Proposed strategies include modular AI coursework, faculty development initiatives, and continuing education.

Periodic assessments of effectiveness — through pre- and post-intervention testing, learner feedback, and curricular benchmarking — are critical to refine these approaches and guarantee that training formats are both pedagogically sound and institutionally sustainable.

unlisted_practices: Integrate foundational AI education into medical training across pre-, undergraduate, graduate, and continuing medical education.
Develop scalable, open-access, asynchronous AI education modules co-developed by multiple stakeholders to overcome infrastructure and expertise barriers in low-resource settings.
Form international collaborations, multilingual platforms, and public-private partnerships to broaden access to AI education.
Adapt AI educational materials to cross-cultural differences in ideologies, languages, and disease pathologies.
Invest in internet access, computers, and digitization to enable AI education in Latin America.
Regulators should provide guidance for developing and implementing AI learning mechanisms that maintains data integrity and ethical use.

Design competency-based AI curricula covering basic AI knowledge, social and ethical implications, workflow analysis, AI-enhanced clinical encounters, evidence-based evaluation, and practice-based learning.
Evaluate AI education using structured approaches such as the Kirkpatrick model rather than relying only on learner satisfaction or immediate knowledge gains.
Funders should prioritize regional AI literacy initiatives.

screen.reason: Viewpoint article discussing AI literacy in medical education across the Americas and proposing strategies for equitable implementation.
